title: Pageable activation tiling and cooperative kernel preempt scheduler to reduce GPU working set
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Reduce peak GPU workspace by ~25% for long-context streaming workloads via movable activation tiles and new preemptive kernel scheduler. Backwards compatible; config opt-in behind runtime flag.
description:
Motivation: Large-context streaming cases and some batched workloads were causing unbounded growth of the GPU working set due to monolithic activation allocation and conservative kernel scheduling. This PR introduces a pageable activation tiling layout and a cooperative kernel preemption scheduler to keep active GPU memory bounded while preserving end-to-end latency targets.

Summary of changes: Implements a lightweight OS-like paging layer for activations (tile units ~64KB) that allows lazy page-in and eviction of cold tiles; introduces cooperative kernel preemption points so long-running kernels yield control to page-in hot tiles without full kernel termination; updates KV cache manager to pin small hot windows and integrate with tile eviction policy; adds batching compatibility so continuous-batching keeps prefetched tiles pinned for expected next requests. All changes are feature-flagged behind runtime config `GPU_PAGEABLE_TILING` and `COOP_PREEMPT_SCHEDULER` and default to OFF for now.

Implementation details: 1) runtime/memory/paging.{cc,hh}: new pageable allocator that splits activations into fixed-size tiles, maintains a two-tier LRU (tile-level hotset + activation metadata). 2) runtime/kernel/scheduler.cpp: cooperative preempt scheduler that instruments safe yield points in attention and MLP kernels; uses lightweight state checkpoint so kernels can resume without full restart. 3) runtime/kv_cache/kv_manager.py: KV cache now tracks tile residency and charges pin cost back to routing decision. 4) continuous batching glue updated to prefetch next-request tiles when batch composition is stable for 2+ requests. 5) tests/perf and benchmarks added.

Testing & validation: Unit tests for allocator invariants and tile eviction; microbenchmarks for page-in latency; integration tests validating correctness of resumed kernels (deterministic outputs compared to baseline); production perf canary run on dedicated pool (see perf summary).

Rollout plan: landed behind feature flags. After merge we'll run a 48h canary on dedicated-xx region with 10% traffic and monitor token latency p50/p95, page-in latency histogram, and memory high-water marks. If stable, flip default to ON for Dedicated customers and enable opt-in for Hosted with per-tenant guardrails.

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids aggressive compression and instead focuses on predictable memory bounds. Follow-ups planned: adaptive tile sizing, intra-GPU prefetch heuristics, and kernel codegen hooks to reduce resume cost.

perf_results: Canary on dedicated-xx: average GPU high-water mark reduced by 24-28% across long-context workloads (8k-32k tokens). p95 token latency increase < 2.5% for most models; a few heavy-attention kernels saw +4% which we mitigated by adjusting prefetch window.
